title: The kelipa comes before the fruit: the opposition, the breaking, Nogah, and the siyum on the book

lectures.id: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

overview: Chapter 54 finishes the book with the kelipa, the shell that protects a growing fruit and is discarded once the fruit is ready. The kelipa comes from the shevira, the breaking of the vessels, which mixed good and bad. Whatever comes out of the essence has an opposite, so we must work to find the truth; concealment and tzimtzum come before every light. The breaking was in the middos of bina, not in chachma. The kelipa also has the form of Adam Beliyaal, the wild man who does whatever he wants. The Nogah of the kelipa is self-awareness: in Atzilus it has no bad in it, but in Beriya it turns into self-interest, in Yetzira into accusation, and in Asiya into harm. The jealousy of the original snake is ego, a little bit bad. The leech and the three impure kelipos are bad, and the wicked who are bad to themselves will not be refined until Moshiach. The chapter closes with the siyum: each person has an inner G-dly essence, and we help others because it is good for them.

terms.gloss: the shell or peel: the protective outer layer that grows first and is discarded once the fruit is ready; the force that opposes holiness. Plural *kelipos*.
the breaking of the vessels, after which good and bad were mixed; a good thing taken out of its context turns bad
contraction: the concealment that comes before every light
the emotional attributes, such as love, fear and anger; the breaking was in the middos of bina
the outer side of a thing, as opposed to its inner essence (penimiyus)
accusation: the Nogah of Yetzira accuses a person of not really meaning his service
the wild man of the kelipa: the self-image of one who does whatever he wants, without a yoke
the good part of the kelipa: pure self-awareness with no bad in it at Atzilus, which turns to ego and self-interest in the lower worlds
the highest of the four worlds, where the Nogah has no bad in it
the second world, where the Nogah turns good done for oneself into self-interest
the third world, where the Nogah is half bad and works as accusation
the lowest of the four worlds, where the Nogah is mostly bad

sections.title: What the kelipa is: the shell of a fruit, from the breaking of the vessels
sections.summary: A *kelipa* takes its name from the peel of a fruit, a protective layer that is the waste in everything. It comes from the mixture of good and bad that followed the *shevira*.

blocks.text: *Tanya* has fifty-four chapters if the introduction counts, and the Torah has fifty-four *parshiyos*. The Alter Rebbe sat in prison for fifty-three days, because of the fifty-three chapters, after being offered prison or death. The Mitteler Rebbe said his father was given that choice and left him the other, and he died at fifty-four. He does not know what it means, but it is significant.

blocks.title: Fifty-four

blocks.text: He thinks the simple lesson is that the Rebbeim had *mesiras nefesh* to teach Chassidus, which is why the Alter Rebbe went to prison. They gave it to us, so we take it off the shelf and learn it. Rebbe Rashab said that he took chassidim who were just born and made them people who grew into being chassidim through their own work. Chassidim who learn Chassidus turn paper Chassidus into living Chassidus, which does more for the Rebbe than the Rebbe does for them. In his view the main lesson is that the wellsprings go outward to us, and we must learn it and live it.

blocks.text: The chapter now traces how the *kelipos* descend through *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*. The last chapter covered the worlds, and that even the *kelipos* are *batel* to G-d; now the focus is the *kelipos* themselves.

blocks.text: A big professor explains something to a small child, who hears the words but does not understand them, or to someone not on the level of the lecture. It is like listening to a language you do not understand. That is the general *mashal*.

blocks.text: The *nimshal*: everything is created from G-d's essence, so everything has intrinsic value and an intrinsic connection to Him, and His love for us is higher than anything we do. A child shown unconditional love may think he can do whatever he likes. That is the *shevira*: we see that everything has G-dly value, and we enjoy things as separate, not in their context. That creates the mixture of good and bad.

blocks.text: G-d made the world as a puzzle or a challenge, so that we work it out ourselves with our *avoda* and it becomes really ours. At first it is easy to misunderstand.

blocks.text: The seven kings of *Tohu* died and fell below, because the middos could not contain the light. The light withdrew, and the vessels fell with a residue of light that remained. Those are the sparks we speak of, the 288 sparks, and they create the *kelipos*.

blocks.text: Why 288? The Rebbe answers simply, in a letter: seventy-two times four, for the four spellings of G-d's name, *Ayin Beis*, *SaG*, *MaH* and *BaN*. The Arizal has a fuller *chashbon* on each: at a certain level the *shevira* takes place, and everything from there down falls. Counted up, it is 288.

sections.title: The shell comes before the fruit: it protects, then it is discarded
sections.summary: The *kelipa* is first, as the shell is first on any fruit. It is not bad in itself: it protects a growing thing and is cast off when it is ready.

blocks.text: A shell is not a bad thing. It serves a purpose as a protective layer, and eventually it is cast off.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: Like the *chashmal* of *bina* and the *levushim* we talked about earlier: a parent gives a little child rules to keep him safe, not to touch fire, play with fire or drive. As you grow you need those restrictions less, since you understand what is behind them and can set your own boundaries, and in some ways do what you could not before. A teenager is in between: he still needs boundaries, but must learn to get beyond them.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.title: The rules a parent sets

blocks.text: Becoming a *bar or bat mitzva* means becoming an adult: not just doing what you are told, but having a sense of what is right yourself.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: Shimon and Levi, rescuing Dina, show the idea. Their attack on Shechem was hasty, but they did not ask what to do: they sensed it could not be allowed, and were willing to sacrifice.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.title: Shimon and Levi at Shechem

blocks.text: That is the fruit, the inner G-dly voice of right and wrong. Around it is the *kelipa*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: Our bodies have survival instincts: the four *yesodos*, fire, water, air and earth, which *Tanya* discusses from the Arizal, and which the animal soul and the body each have. They are the source of most bad *middos*, but not totally bad: they help us survive. A craving for tasty food gets us to eat; without it, a person would suffer serious malnutrition.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: The *chachamim* wanted to get rid of the *yetzer hara*, but were not sure it was a good thing, so they locked him up. It says the chickens stopped laying eggs, and people stopped reproducing: without desire the world cannot function. So they blinded him and let him go. It took away two things: the desire for idolatry became a desire for money, and the desire for incest was removed.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.title: The yetzer hara locked up

blocks.text: All these drives we call the *yetzer hara* were created by G-d for a purpose, and we see them out of context. G-d gave them to help us survive long enough to get a brain and mature enough to appreciate what is right. Parents, education and mentors create a good environment for that. If not, the *kelipa* protects us until we get a moment of clarity and grow up.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: Like any fruit, the shell grows first. A flower is fertilized, the fruit begins to form, and at first it is mainly shell. Inside the shell, which is like a womb, the seeds are like little children developing. When the fruit is ripe and the seeds are ready, the fruit bursts open, the seeds come out, and the shell is no longer needed, or when someone is going to eat it.

sections.title: Every expansion has an opposite: the opposition is built into creation
sections.summary: Whatever expands from the essence has an opposing force that also comes from the essence, and so does every delight, reason and middah once it is expressed outside the essence.

blocks.text: He is going to explain the root. So far: the *kelipos* come from the *shevira* and the seven kings of *Tohu*. They are called a shell because, like the shell before the fruit or the placenta, they serve a purpose and are discarded once they are no longer needed.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: Pleasure has its opposite too: pain. *Oneg* and *nega* are the same letters reversed, as *Sefer Yetzira* says. Take a good thing out of its context and it becomes bad. That is the *shevira*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: Every creature has a G-d-given nature; living in line with it expresses our essence, which is pleasure. A child is immature and does not know who he is; a mature adult or mentor can see who he really is.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: Rambam's *mashal*: a child asks why he should learn to read, and says he would rather go and play. The adult sees that by the nature of his soul he must be curious and keep growing. The child does not see it, and if he does not develop his true self he will end up stifled and in pain. So you make rules, with rewards and punishments. Those are a protective shell, and they are discarded once he is mature. You do not want to force him with a threat or bribe him; you want him to appreciate the intrinsic value, because that is who he is.

blocks.text: What expands from the essence has an opposing force, also from the essence. Once a thing goes outside the essence, where it never changes, it becomes a system to express itself, as with *Adam Kadmon*. So there can be a disconnect: as the book says in chapters 18 and 19, a person does not always feel like learning or business, even when it is associated with who he is but is not essential to him.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: The test is whether a thing ever changes, or is always there.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: You can see this with *mesiras nefesh*, though not always, since it can get attached to something external. It is not a simple answer, but you know it when you see it. Learning to see this is one of the main things in learning this book. Some things never change: certain innate human things and innate Jewish things, which have not changed through all times, places and generations.

blocks.text: Even the highest delight and will, which are essential, have an opposing force, as with *Keser*, the intermediary between the essence and everything outside it. As soon as a person associates his delight with something outside himself, the opposite appears.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: If you attach your pleasure to something outside you, like learning or eating, which is not essential, it can be withheld, and then you feel pain. Or something can block what you want, the opposite of pleasure. That is *tza'ar* and *yisurin*, pain and suffering.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: The same goes for intellect: it is created, not essential, and its truth comes from the axioms you plug into it, so you can argue the opposite. That is why you can never win an argument with a fundamentalist, and it can be very frustrating.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: Even in *kedusha*, the *Baal Shem Tov* spoke to a person: he explained one position until the person agreed, then explained the opposite. He kept going back and forth, because each level down the *seder hishtalshelus* flips, and it can go on endlessly.

blocks.title: The Baal Shem Tov explains both ways

blocks.text: Moshe, receiving the Torah, saw forty-nine reasons for *tamei* and forty-nine for *tahor*: intellect, delight and will cannot be the source of truth, since each has an opposite.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: The same goes for the *middos*: you can love a good thing or a bad thing. And for thought, speech and action: you can think one way and think another, or speak the opposite.

sections.title: Concealment comes first: G-d built the world so that we must work for the truth
sections.summary: The opposite is not an accident. Concealment and *tzimtzum* come before every light, so the first impression is wrong and we have to do *avoda* to find the essence of things.

blocks.text: This is how G-d created the world: everything has an opposite, to show us that these things are not essential.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: G-d creates holiness, Torah and mitzvos, to connect us to Him, and the ability to choose and enjoy the opposite, so we can try both and do both. One is my true G-dly self; the other is not. That brings a person to *teshuva*, to his real essence, since he can have both opposites.

blocks.text: Coming to Rosh HaShana: a king sent his son away to study in far lands, to be exposed to life beyond the palace. blocks.text: In everything that is not an essence, G-d specifically creates an opposite: the waste and the *kelipa*, the shell, the peel and the concealment, which always comes first.

blocks.text: Like a puzzle, where your first intuition is wrong and you must work to uncover the answer. So too with us: our intuition about who we are and what makes us happy is wrong, and we must do *avoda* to discover who we really are and what the world is.

blocks.text: As in the sciences, understanding reality takes work, and our first intuition is too superficial. Kids do not know what will make them happy, and the Disney films about running away from home and eloping do not make people happy either. What is presented to people is a superficial idea of happiness. Whether we learn the easy way or the hard way, we have to learn who we really are and what reality is.

sections.title: The breaking was in the middos of bina, not in chachma; the kelipa of chachma is cunning
sections.summary: The true mixture of good and bad came only from the lower middos of bina. Chachma itself was not broken, but its outer side fell and became external wisdom, which is cunning when cut off from the inner truth.

blocks.text: The main *shevira* that made a true mixture of good and bad was only in *SaG*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: The breaking was only from the level of *SaG*, the seven lower *middos* of *bina*. He lists *Ayin Beis*, *SaG*, *MaH* and *BaN*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: The *middos* of the intellect give birth to the *middos* of the heart, and those can be negative. With an improper understanding, a person thinks something will make him happy, or that he should love, hate or get angry about something. With a correct understanding he matures and realizes that what he should care about is different.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: The Rebbe's *ma'amar* goes through each *middos* of *Sefiras HaOmer*, showing how each is in *kedusha* and *kelipa*, and how to transform it. *Sefiras HaOmer* takes place in the *middos* of *bina*. Learning the right perspective changes how we feel: the *mocha* rules over the heart.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: This ties to *Adam Kadmon*, which he says corresponds to *SaG*: your inner *ratzon kadum*, your essential desire, is matched with something outside. That automatically creates something imperfect, so there is good and bad, and always an opposite, because there is always a *klipa*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: Even the Rambam, in the *Moreh Nevuchim*, says that every *mashal* has parts that fit the *nimshal* and parts that are extraneous circumstances, which you must set aside.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: Whenever you express something essential in something external, you get a mixture of good and bad, and this happens mainly in the *middos* of *bina*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: This gives rise to actual bad *middos*, such as anger: a person ties his whole identity to something and gets angry about it. If he understood that G-d runs the world and these things do not matter, he would not get angry.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: Murder, a bad craving, and negative loves and fears: a person loves what he should not, or fears what he should not fear.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: The Rebbe speaks of the great and awesome desert: intimidated by the world and the nations, we are afraid in our own skin and cannot be who we are. That creates *galus*. When the fear stops, we are free.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: Boasting, *hisp'arus*, comes from measuring yourself by how others perceive you, instead of feeling self-confident and knowing who you are. It also means boasting about bad things, or about knowing them: one sign of that negative mentality is that teenagers and adults involved in bad things take pride in it.

blocks.text: In *chachma* there was no *shevira*. *Chochma* is seeing the truth for what it is, before you interpret it, so there is no room for anything wrong.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: The same is true of your inner desires, the *ratzon kadum*, which is the level of *chachma*. *Shabbos*, as we said, is like that: a celebration of our essential connection to G-d and to the people around us, not about accomplishing anything. A baby has intrinsic value and cannot do anything wrong, so there is no *shevira* there.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: Only the *chitzoniyus* of *Abba* and *Imma* fell, and then you apply your understanding incorrectly. No bad questions, but wrong applications: a bridge built wrong collapses, like not doing your homework. That is the root of external wisdoms.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: External wisdoms are sciences taken out of their context and made into a whole *chachma* of their own, separate from their purpose; people forget their basic assumptions. Occam's razor is one of the most fundamental things science rests on, but it is not an objective thing.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: Where does that come from? From an innate sense that some things are beautiful, and an innate G-dly need to know that things are a certain way. So it does matter: it is connected to morality and to how we live.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: He is not saying there is not a lot of truth in these things, or that they are wrong. But there is no purely objective thing: behind everything there is a philosophy, axioms and beliefs, and an interpretation is people understanding things, not the truth. External wisdom is no source of truth unless it is connected to the inner *chachma*, which guides it to the right place.

blocks.text: A little child sneaks a cookie from the jar, rationalizes it, and disconnects from the inner knowledge that it is not what he should be doing.

blocks.text: True *chachma* is the *pnimiyus*, which is connected. Disconnected, it becomes sneakiness, trickery or sophistry: using good debate skills to prove anything, and it tries to deceive. That is what "I am *chachma*, my neighbor is cunning" means.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: Someone asked what makes something propaganda. He defines it as trying to get someone to make an emotional decision, by connecting to essential things so that it overrides his *sechel*. That is manipulation.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: Lavan was a trickster: *chachma* of *kelipa*, very smart but smart at working out how to deceive. Sometimes this *kelipa* can affect people: someone who learns a lot of Torah can become very smart, and must be careful not to use it to evade taxes and end up in jail.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: Sometimes people use *chachma* this way, even Torah: Shimon and Levi were using it, and Levi came up with legal excuses why they should kill Yosef.

blocks.text: When a person's perspective is wrong, it perverts even *chachma*, and his pleasure attaches to external things he enjoys without realizing they are valuable only as an expression of who he is.

blocks.text: The Rebbe in *Kuntres Inyana shel Toras HaChassidus* explains *modeh ani*: on the level of *peshat* we thank G-d for life and blessings; from the level of the *yechida*, the value of my life comes from being a *chelek Elokah mimaal mamash*, an opportunity, a *kli* to express who I really am. sections.title: Adam Beliyaal: the wild man of the kelipa, and the struggle against him
sections.summary: The kelipa has a form of a man, called Adam Beliyaal: the self-image of one who does whatever he wants. Yaakov wrestles with it, and the struggle is to see the truth from inside and outside, and to grow out of it.

blocks.text: Just as in holiness *tikun* is arranged into the form of a man, so in the *kelipos* there is also a form of a man.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: This is *Adam Beliyaal*, the wild man without a yoke: the archetype of most Hollywood heroes, like James Bond, who are beyond the law and can murder, steal and rape, and whatever they do is good.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

sensitivity.reason: The word "rape" in a list of what the wild man does, and a jab at Hollywood heroes as a type of film hero (a profession).
sensitivity.publishable: This is *Adam Beliyaal*, the wild man without a yoke: the archetype of most action-movie heroes, like James Bond, who are beyond the law and can murder, steal and hurt people, and whatever they do is good.

blocks.text: The wild man's self-image is a mistaken idea from the broken *kelipa*: he can do whatever he wants and it will be good, and he need not listen to anybody. Like a little child, he thinks what makes him happy is doing what he wants.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: What you must teach a child is discipline: you can do whatever you want, but it will be bad for you, and you won't like it. Know who you are and how the world works: some things do not work in the world, or with other people.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: A good parent teaches a child that, because you love him, you give more and put up with more; but others will not put up with it. They will not give him what he wants, and might punch him or fire him. So in childhood, in a safe setting, you simulate it: "If you talk to me that way, I won't give you what you want," and he learns to say please and thank you.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.title: The child who learns the limits

blocks.text: The *kelipa* thinks I can say and do what I want, and people will just give it to me. Our culture in general today has been educated in this and is insulated from its consequences: we bend over backwards to give people what they want, and lie to them to make them feel good. That perpetuates the *kelipa*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

sensitivity.reason: A sweeping jab at present-day culture ("our culture in general today"): a remark about a group, not about the idea.
sensitivity.publishable: The *kelipa* thinks I can say and do what I want, and people will just give it to me. Many people today have been educated in this and are insulated from its consequences: we bend over backwards to give people what they want, and lie to them to make them feel good. That perpetuates the *kelipa*.

blocks.text: This is the *Zeir Anpin* of the *kelipa*, its *middos*: Yaakov's wrestling, which the verse says was like the angel of Esav. Yaakov is the good person, and he must wrestle with the opposition, the idea of Esav: I can just do what I want.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: There are two sources of truth, inside and outside. To see a person's nature you look inside, and to see it clearly you need a proper life.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: A *chacham*, a *navi* or a *rebbe*, or just a mature person, can look at a child and know he will want to learn to read. It is hard to convince the child, but as an adult you have that obligation.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: The external side: G-d set consequences into the world. He favors having a family and blessing with children; certain behaviors won't bring blessing.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: There's a big epidemic now: a lot of modern cultures are not having kids.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

sensitivity.reason: A sweeping remark about "modern cultures" (a jab at present-day cultures, softened in STYLE terms).
sensitivity.publishable: There's a big epidemic now: a lot of people are not having kids.

blocks.text: Nothing is new under the sun: people have made most mistakes already, as the verse says, ask your father and your elders.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: The internet and AI are new forms of old challenges. The struggle is within us; the outside world is a different *levush*. Do I know who I am and why I am here, or do I let other things define and control me?

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: In *Yafe Sha'ah Achas*, a person infected with the *kelipa* of *Amalek* is like a spoiled child: told he is hurting himself, he says, "It's my life, I can do what I want." Seeing that takes *avoda*. Like an addict, he cannot see that he is hurting himself, though everybody else can.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.title: The spoiled child

blocks.text: You cannot simply convince people: if somebody is confused, he is confused. But if you love someone, you make rules, laws, police and teachers, and a couple of years later they come around and say, "You're right."

sections.title: Nogah: no bad in Atzilus, but feeling one's own good turns to ego; in Beriya, good done for oneself
sections.summary: The *kelipas Nogah* of *Atzilus* is pure self-awareness, with no bad in it, but when a person feels his own good qualities, that feeling is already a *kelipa* and leads to showing off. The *Nogah* of *Beriya* takes good deeds to self-interest, and the show-off who wants to be superior makes his good into something bad.

blocks.text: In general there are ten *sefiros* of *kelipas Nogah* in the four worlds.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: Now he zooms in on the difference between the *kelipos* of each world, and how one leads to the next. The Rebbe's *ma'amar* "Lo Tihiyeh Meshakhla" goes through the descent step by step: how a person sinks into evil.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

phrases.he: ודרך כלל יש בחינת עשר ספירות דקליפת נוגה באבי"ע
phrases.en: in general there are ten *sefiros* of *kelipas Nogah*, in the four worlds of *Atzilus*, *Beriah*, *Yetzirah* and *Asiyah*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: In *Atzilus* the *kelipas Nogah* has no bad in it, as the verse says, *lo yagurcha ra*; only the *yesh* is most felt.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: The *kelipas Nogah* is only self-awareness, like the *eitz hadaas*, where people became aware that they were naked.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: Take a person who does a kindness and thinks nothing of it, like a rescuer from a burning building who says anybody would have done it. Another feels, look at me, I'm a great guy, and wants his name on the building. Putting a name on a building is not bad in itself; the point is that he feels it and shows off.

blocks.text: In *Shaar HaEmunah* he gives a *mashal* for the revelation of the *yechida*: a child dancing, not self-conscious at all, who does not care who is watching.

blocks.text: Then they shift from *penimiyus* to *chitzoniyus*, from being themselves to wondering how to get the reaction. That creates the *kelipa*; they lose it to a certain degree.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/054 Shaar HaYichud ch 54 with siyum.mp3

blocks.text: Self-awareness is a very useful tool: without it we would behave badly, our manners would be poor. So the *kelipa* is a shell that protects and trains a person.

blocks.text: But if you don't grow out of it, you stay stifled, a slave to these things. Mature, regain that youth, plug into your *yechida* and be yourself. The same goes for all a person's *middos*: he feels them very self-aware, and that is the *kelipas Nogah* of *Atzilus*.

sections.title: The jealousy of the original snake, the leech, and the impure kelipos; then the siyum
sections.summary: The jealousy of the original snake is ego, a little bit bad. In the *Nogah* of *Yetzira* it is half bad, an accusation like the *Satan*'s, and in *Asiya* it is mostly bad: people find a holy excuse for harm. The *kelipa* is compared to a leech, and below it are the three impure *kelipos*, pure bad with no good mixed in. The book ends with the siyum: thanks to G-d, and the point that each person has an inner G-dly essence and we help others because it is good for them.

blocks.text: This is the jealousy of the original snake, the *yetzer hara*: ego, *yesh l'garmei*, a little bit bad.
